Some things are illegible but I believe that I did read this, and that's why I'm so clear on everything, because I'm not familiar with this document. I don't know what its legal power was. I repeat, there were some inter-municipality meetings, they were in Sanski Most, not in Korcanica, I wasn't there, but they did not have any legal power, they did not have any power whatsoever, at least those meetings that I attended. I'm really not familiar with this particular kind of meeting. I'm not aware of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. If I may just ask the witness to intervene here. There appears to be a line missing in the English translation of this. It is the line that appears above the name and surname in function of and location and the date. There is a handwritten three words. Perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just -- what is missing? Oh, just at the --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The top. Very top.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the very top.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, and perhaps that could be read into the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you could read that. Mr. Pasic, you see that on the very top of that page, three words of which the first one seems to be not complete. Could you read what it says in your own language so that we --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try. It seems that it reads, "The second inter --" I don't know whether this is an S, municipality, full stop, agreement. I believe that this is the second inter-municipality briefing, and then it says, Korcanica, 14 June 1992. That's on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for assisting us. Please proceed, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I'm very near the end, being aware of the time constraints.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Tab 23, please. Page 4 in the B/C/S, two paragraphs at the top of that page, immediately before section 3 begins. So the two top paragraphs, could you quickly read those to yourself. They will be found at page 3 in the English. You were asked about them in part earlier. Summarising, they talk about vindictiveness and revenge resulting from the enemy closing its rank, increasing shortage of basic food, rising prices, poverty, social destitution, shortages of electricity and lack of fuel paralysing the economy as a whole. Were things as bad as that for the Serb population of your municipality at this time in June of 1992, Mr. Pasic?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already spoken about that. The situation was difficult for everybody; for the Serbs equally as for the Muslims. There was no electricity, there was no fuel, there was no oil. And this speaks enough. The situation was alarming. It was extraordinary. But it was the same across the board, in the territories inhabited by the Serbs as well as by the Muslims. We were all struck by this crisis. The times were hard. And the little food that we had we couldn't preserve it because there was no electricity. The food could not be stored. We reached very hard times, but the situation was the same for everybody in the municipality of Novi Grad.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Thank you for the Court's indulgence, bearing in mind the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have no further questions for you, Mr. Pasic, which means that this concludes your testimony in this Court. One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Still some documents need numbers but we are already far over time so we could deal with that tomorrow morning -- tomorrow in the afternoon. Mr. Pasic, I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague, not only once but even two times, and I'm at least glad that we could finish today. Thanking you for answering questions of both the parties and the Bench, and I wish you as safe a trip home again as you had last time. Madam Usher, could you please --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we turn into private session for just a very brief period of time.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to thank the interpreters and the technicians for their assistance 15 minutes beyond the time we should have stopped. We will adjourn and we will reconvene tomorrow in the afternoon, quarter past 2, Courtroom II? Yes. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 17th day of January, 2006, at 2.15 p.m.
